title: Build and use an LL(1) table
description: You can follow how grammar sets guide a parser with an explicit symbol stack.

steps.description: FIRST collects possible starting terminals. first_of_string carries that calculation across a sequence that may include empty productions.
FOLLOW collects terminals that can appear after a nonterminal. The loop propagates new entries until the sets stop growing.
The table builder places productions under starting terminals and uses FOLLOW for empty choices. It records competing entries as conflicts.
The driver starts with the end marker and start symbol. A matching terminal pops the stack and advances input.

steps.question: Why does the driver push a production in reversed order?
steps.answer: The leftmost production symbol must become the next stack top.

steps.description: Nonterminal entries expand the stack. Missing entries or mismatched terminals return failure; the supplied grammar separates expression and term tiers.
The final section constructs the table and asks the driver to parse the supplied token sequence. It prints the table, conflict report, action trace, and acceptance status.
